pages.text:
Barclays Interview and Internship Experience 
30th August, 2018 
 
 
Barclays had conducted campus interviews for Internship and Full Time hiring at VJTI in August
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
2018. They have a relatively easy process of selection and familiarity with basic coding is sufficient
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
to clear it successfully. Following were the rounds conducted for hiring interns. 
 
Round 1: Online Test 
 
The online test consisted of 3 sections: 
1.
Quantitative: Basic math and logical ability questions which you regularly encounter in
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
olympiads. The level of math is not above 10th grade and is very easy but the number of
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
questions is high which makes it slightly harder. (30 mins) 
2.
Verbal: Basic English questions like “fill in the blanks”, comprehension etc. (typical AMCAT
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
questions) (30 mins) 
3.
Coding: 2 questions of beginner level but everyone has a different set of questions. 
1 of my question was to find the last digit of a^b for large values of a and b. 
The other one was easy as well. Everyone who had basic experience in coding did not take
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
more than 10 minutes to solve both the questions. 
 
Round 2: Technical Interview 
 
After the online test around 30-35 people were shortlisted for the interviews. My interview began with
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
a small introduction. After this the interviewer asked me to walk him through my resume. I explained
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
all the projects I had mentioned in my resume and my extra-curricular activities. The interviewer also
 
 
  
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
posed some technical queries to me relating to my project. After this he asked me to write a few
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
simple codes in Java/C++(choice was given).  
 
After this he started asking situational questions designed to introduce some difficult choices and
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
test how I would react. Banks usually conduct this round to gauge the professional fitness of the
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
candidate. There is no right answer to these questions, just try to give ethically and morally sound
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
responses and you should be good to go. 
 
Barclays, as is the case with most banks, was looking for students with sound knowledge in
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Database management systems, as well as a good foundation in any major programming language,
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
  
 
 
 
 
preferably Java. They did not focus much on data structures or complex programming skills as most
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
of their profiles relate to development and testing. 
 
Round 3: HR interview 
 
Barclays expects the candidates to know a bit about the company and they ask you questions about
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
the values of Barclays. You can look up the full form of RISES on the Barclays website and prepare
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
for questions on the same. The interviewer might ask you about examples of RISES in your life. You
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
just have to convince the interviewer that you understand the meaning of every word in the acronym,
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
and that you try to apply it in your personal/professional life.

After these questions end the interviewer will inquire whether you have any queries. Make it a point
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
to ask a question so as to show your interest towards joining the company. This leaves a lasting
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
impression on your interviewer. 
 
 
 
Result: 
 
After this round the results were declared and a total of 12 people were selected from CS and IT.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The results were skewed in favour of IT branch (8 from IT, 4 from comps). 
 
 
Internship Experience: 
 
The internship began on 20th May, a few days after my end semester exams. However only 10 out
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
of the 12 people selected had received their offer letters. This was highly unprofessional from
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Barclays and the 2 remaining people had joined almost 5 weeks after I did. Also the old office did not
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
  
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
have enough space and most of us were not allotted a permanent desk. Instead there was a rotation
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
  
 
schedule where in the full time employees would take turns to work from home one day of the week
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
and we would sit in their places for the day. However this should not be a problem anymore since
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
they have shifted to a new office building. 
 
I had been assigned an interesting project related to Optical Character Recognition (OCR). But I was
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
very lucky in this. Many of my friends were stuck on testing projects and were asking to be shifted to
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
other teams. This is the harsh truth about working in a bank. If you are lucky, you will get to work on
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
   
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
a challenging and engaging project. It is also possible that you might have to work in testing which in
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
  
comparison is not as fun. Also the desktops I had to work on came with Windows 7 which is again a
  
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
  
  
pretty big disadvantage of working at banks. Banks are reluctant when it comes to accepting new
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
technologies before their security has been proven. This is why it is hard to get work on modern
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
operating systems and technology stacks and there is a tedious procedure for installation of
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
necessary software which eats up a lot of valuable time. 
 
We were also encouraged to meet with Directors and Managing Directors (MDs) of various
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
departments as part of their overall intern development. We set up meetings with them, asked them
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
about their roles and career paths and gained insightful information. We were also lucky to have a
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
meeting with the BX India co-CEO, Mr. Praveen Kumar and the Chief Security Officer Mr. Tim
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
McNulty, and leave with the inspirational session in mind. In addition to this, we also took part in one
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
of the regular social drives that take place in the company. 
 
The office location is in Kharadi, Pune and Barclays provides transport to and from your
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
residence.Travelling in Pune otherwise is very costly owing to the traffic and poor public transport.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Apart from the large stipend they offered an additional 25k a month as a relocation benefit which
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
  
 
 
 
makes it easy to find comfortable accommodation like OYO rooms (Hostels and PGs are horrible
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
and squalid in Pune).

Pre-Placement Offer: Barclays conducts two reviews with your line-manager and here is your
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
chance to discuss your position on the pre-placement offer. If you believe that you have a good shot
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
at securing better placement in the final year placements or you hate working with archaic tech I
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
would recommend you to insinuate that you do not want a PPO. This will ensure that you do not run
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
into any problems with the TPO of VJTI. The recently formulated rule by TPO, which states that you
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
can reject a PPO of under 10lakh CTC if you think you have a shot at receiving a better offer via
 
  
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
  
 
 
  
 
 
 
campus, is something you can use to your advantage. However if you are happy with the easy going
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
nature of your life in the 2 months you have worked there or if you want to prepare for a Master’s
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
  
 
program in a foreign country I would recommend that you work for a year or two at Barclays to build
 
  
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
your profile and take the requisite tests(GRE, TOEFL, IELTS etc). Barclays is an internationally
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
recognized brand and this will reflect supremely on your MS applications. Getting a good project at
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
Barclays is really not in your hands and you cannot apply for a change of department until you have
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
worked there for over a year. Do keep this in mind before making a decision. 
 
I have tried to answer most of the FAQs with respect to the internship and I wish you all the best for
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
your future!
